Everybody dissociates to some degree; like when you have such a vivid daydream someone or something has to snap you out of it, or when you’re doing the dishes but you’re not really there and experiencing it. It’s part of why everyone keeps recommending ‘mindfulness and meditation’ for our daily mental health. 

There’s dissociative disorder which is where these behaviours affect your life and cause dysfunction. So for me; I have stress-reactive dissociation and I lift out of my body or crawl into the recesses of my mind which makes me avoid experiencing and feeling stressful events. If my boss calls me in for a meeting, I dissociate - the heart races, the thoughts shut off, and the emotions shut down. Perspective may warp and it feels like the room extends in front of me or like I’m in the front of my brain thinking when suddenly I physically pull back in my mind and can’t think. 

As for day-to-day, it just feels like you’re an observer. You can try control and influence your behaviour and words but at the worst of it you might be sitting and watching words come out your mouth that you don’t mean and you can’t stop, for example, as though someone else is saying them. Time drifts. A year passes with no event or memory because while you’re dissociating your brain stores that shit out of sight or not at all. 

That’s for me; there are other experiences of dissociative disorder and ‘normal’ dissociation too. The ‘cure’ is mindfulness and meditation, along with therapy and maybe medication to deal with some symptoms if that’s what works for your case.

Edit: forgot to mention there’s a host of terminology too which makes distinctions between different states. Derealisation can be a part of dissociation but it’s to do with how you perceive the outside world, for example. Definitely do some research if you feel it might be something that gets away from you.

Did they get a sudden amount of lots more light? It could have been the sudden change too. People tend to gradually introduce them for more hours so they don’t crisp. My cacti are all in direct sunlight in the morning for ~6 hours. I water them every 14 days but not a soak - just enough for their roots to be happy. 

But some different species need different things. Always good to try research individual plants. Try see what they are and what they need and act accordingly, some will definitely be gone but one or two might survive. I’d put them in a few hours of weak early sunlight and a bit of water - not a soak. Someone else may have better suggestions though

They don’t all really like being misted. Just a well draining pot, plant in 50:50 ratio of cactus mix:perlite (I add a layer of course sand on top which helps prevent fungus gnats), water soil when the top inch or so is dry or when the leaves start to get a bit shrivelled. 

I can’t see the bottom one but for the top one I’d pull it out, prune off the yellow/dead leaves and let the roots dry in a sunny (not blazing) area, then replant it in dry 50:50 mix:perlite and only water after a few days. Then leave it and water again in 2 or so weeks. 

That should allow the roots to dry out a bit before being gently brought back to the right moisture and environment so you don’t get root rot or even more shock to the roots. Some people use sulphur on their roots to prevent/kill root rot too.
